ELITE.compositionNote: Elite Pools & Unified Portfolios continue to draw on PIMCO, Loomis Sayles and iAGAM as sub-advisors. The structural change at iAGAM takes effect today: the Asset Allocation team led by Tej Rai and Alex Bellefleur takes over four segregated funds from external managers effective Sep 14/26 (funds renamed, category/risk/objectives unchanged, MER expected to decrease), following Sébastien Mc Mahon's earlier move to Chief Economist, iA Financial Group (May 19/26); no same-day confirmation of completion has been published yet, unsurprising given today is a Sunday. On the PIMCO side, new detail confirms manager Emmanuel Sharef's fund is specifically the PIMCO 60/40 Balanced Income and Growth Fund (~$19B AUM, outperforming 97% of peers over 3 years), with roughly 60% of its equity allocation now Asia-linked (Samsung, SK Hynix, TSMC) as it continues rotating out of 'Magnificent Seven' US tech on the view that AI capex is inflating Big Tech debt burdens while Asia offers more direct 'physical AI buildout' exposure. Loomis Sayles has still not published anything reacting to this week's market moves; its most recent identifiable piece is a mid-year Municipal Sector Outlook (~Aug 4/26), with no fresh September date found. iA Clarington's overall AUM (>$26B, Jul 31/26) and iAGAM's firm-wide AUM ($156B, Jun 30/26) were both carried forward unchanged. The bigger outside story today reversed direction from yesterday's preview: the Iran/GCC/Iraq meeting in Oman meant to negotiate the Strait of Hormuz's future on this same date was postponed 'in the interests of consensus,' with no new date set — a live, unresolved test of the PIMCO and Loomis Sayles sleeves' positioning for continued geopolitical uncertainty, right alongside the internal management change that did land on schedule.
